steps.npc: Hello there! Are you interested in hearing all about crafting?

options.text: How can I train my crafting?

steps.player: How can I train my crafting?

steps.text: If the player has level 1-9 Crafting:

steps.npc: To get started, you might like to try your hand at crafting some armour from cow's leather. There's a tanner just over in Al Kharid who could tan any hides for you.
Once you've managed to get your hand on some kind of leather, you just need a needle and some thread to get to work!
If that doesn't take your fancy, you could try your hand at spinning wool right here on the spinning wheel.
Come to think of it... Farmer Fred, just north of here, sounds like he could use a hand shearing some of his sheep. Maybe you could help him out, and get some practice while you're at it.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: If the player has level 10-19 Crafting:

steps.player: How can I train my crafting?

steps.npc: Lots of budding craftsmen seem to spend their time here spinning Flax into bow strings on the wheel, if that takes your fancy.
Or you might like to try your hand at crafting some armour from cow's leather. There's a tanner just over in Al Kharid who could tan any hides for you.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: If the player has level 20-99 Crafting:
If the player has below 99 Crafting:

steps.npc: Now that you've got a little experience under your belt, the world's your oyster!
I can't help but feel like I should be the one asking you! At this point, the world's your oyster!
If you wanted to try your hand at making some jewellery, you'll want to get your hand on some gold and some kind of gem, with a mould to work with and a chisel at hand.
But if that's not your thing, maybe you'd like to try making some more armour!
Cow's leather's a good place to start, but you can try all other kinds of hides, like a dragon's!
Glass blowing seems to be a popular trade, too. You can forge molten glass from some sand and soda ash, then make all kinds of things using a glass blowing pipe.
Is there anything else you want to know

options.text: What kinds of things can be crafted?

steps.player: What kinds of things can be crafted?

steps.npc: All kinds of things, really! You can make armour from leather, make some pottery, try your hand at glass blowing, make some jewellery, weapons even...
What would you like to hear about?
Sure thing! Most armour you can craft just involves taking a needle and some thread to whatever material you can get your hands on.
You might like to try with different kinds of animal hide, from cows, yaks, snakes, dragons... Or any other sort of fabric you can find!
Some crafty types have started making some leather- covered wooden shields recently, too!
You might find some creatures make for a pretty sturdy helmet, too. The best way to make something like that's just to take a good old chisel to it!
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?
Of course! Pottery's all kind of the same, it just takes a lot of getting used to.
All that there really is to it is getting your hands on some clay, getting it wet and getting to work on a potter's wheel.
Once you've got the shape you want out of it, you want to put it in a pottery oven to fire it up.
The barbarians west of Varrock seem to be pretty keen on their pottery. I'd take a look around there, if you wanted to try it out!
Once you get the hang of it, you can make pots, pie dishes, bowls... You know.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?
Glass blowing? Well, to get started you'll need to get yourself some molten glass. You can make some for yourself by heating sand and soda ash in a furnace.
Once you've got a hold of that, you'll want a glass blowing pipe to blow it out in to shape, before it cools down.
It's not the easiest thing to get to grips with, but it shouldn't be too difficult!
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?
Sure. All it boils down to is a bar of gold or silver, some kind of cut gem if you're feeling fancy, and a mould to help shape the thing.
You can use a chisel to make a gem really shine and sparkle. You wouldn't want to use an uncut one for any jewellery.
Once you've got all of your materials together, you'll want to use a furnace to actually craft whatever it is you're trying to make!
Wizards seem to like enchanting their jewellery to do all kinds of things, too, but I don't know a lot about that.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?
Well, there aren't too many weapons that people tend to craft, but there are a couple worth noting!
Battlestaves are probably the most common. It boils down to fastening an orb of some kind onto the end of a battlestaff.
You do need to get the orb in the first place, though... You can make one through glass blowing, but it's not much use without being charged.
I can't help much with crafting it, though! There's a little more magic involved there than I'm familiar with.
Aside from battlestaves, there are a couple of weapons that people like to make from silver... Sickles and bolts, usually.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?
